subject: Aurelia contracting: output rights, training opt-out & next steps
messages:
From: Beth Keller <beth.keller@aurelia.com>
To: Nikhil Sharma <nikhil_sharma@redwood.com>
Cc: Aurelia Procurement <procurement@aurelia.com>
Date: Fri, 9 Jan 2026 16:12:00 -0800
Subject: Draft order form + a few questions on output ownership and training

Hi Nikhil,

Thanks for sending the OA draft (attached). A few quick items our GC and procurement team flagged that we wanted to confirm before we circulate the redlines:

- Output ownership: the current draft references "outputs" but it's not explicit whether Aurelia would hold title versus a license. We need clarity on whether downstream distribution by our product teams would be unrestricted.
- Training/use of customer data: the draft mentions a feedback license. Does Redwood train models on customer content by default, or only if we opt in? Our policy is to block any training unless explicitly agreed.
- Attribution / derived IP: we want to avoid language that gives Redwood ownership of derivatives or productized functionality that our teams will build on top of outputs.

Attached: Aurelia_OrderForm_v3.pdf. Can your team propose specific language we can give to our legal team to make the review quicker? Also happy to do a short call early next week.

Best,
Beth Keller
Head of Partnerships
Aurelia Health

From: Nikhil Sharma <nikhil_sharma@redwood.com>

Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 9 Jan 2026 17:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Draft order form + a few questions on output ownership and training

Beth — thanks for the note and the attached order form. Appreciate the clarity on Aurelia's policy.

High level from our side: we want to be explicit and pragmatic — minimize legal churn while protecting our model IP and giving customers the assurances they need. Two quick options we can propose to your counsel:

1) Customer-Title approach (preferred by customers who must re-distribute outputs):
   - "Customer retains title to Outputs that consist solely of Customer Content; Redwood grants Customer a perpetual, worldwide, royalty-free license to use Outputs for any internal or commercial purpose."

2) License-with-guardrails approach (preserves some Redwood model IP):
   - "Customer receives a perpetual, non-exclusive, sublicensable license to use Outputs. Customer-owned content remains Customer Content. Redwood shall not use Customer Content to further train or improve Redwood models without Customer's explicit written opt-in."

On training/feedback: we can offer a default 'no-train' stance (Redwood will not use Customer Content for model training) with an optional opt-in feedback clause for teams that want to participate in product-improvement programs.

Looping in Laura and Connor from legal/ops to craft language you can share. I'll attach an internal clause suggestions doc with proposed snippets and a short mutual action plan (timelines) — should speed your GC's review.

Can we schedule a 30-min sync on Mon (1/12) 10:00am PT to walk through?

Thanks,
Nikhil Sharma
Head of GTM — Redwood Inference

Subject: RE: Draft order form + a few questions on output ownership and training

Beth / Nikhil — thanks for the context. I reviewed the attached OA and sketched redline suggestions below. I tried to balance Aurelia's distribution needs with Redwood's need to protect model IP and product telemetry.

Key suggested positions (high-level):

1) Outputs / Title: recommended middle-ground language:
   "Customer retains title to Outputs to the extent such Outputs consist solely of Customer Content. For Outputs that are generated by model transformations incorporating Redwood's confidential model weights or architecture, Customer is granted a perpetual, worldwide, non-exclusive, transferable license to use, reproduce, and distribute such Outputs. This license does not transfer ownership of Redwood's underlying models, weights, or training data."

2) Training / Feedback License:
   - Default: "Redwood will NOT use Customer Content or Outputs to retrain or improve Redwood models.
   - Opt-in program: "Customer may elect to participate in an optional feedback program under a separate agreement which, if executed, will permit Redwood to use de-identified Customer telemetry and selected Customer feedback to improve models."

3) Telemetry and aggregate usage data:
   - "Redwood may collect aggregated, non-identifiable telemetry necessary to operate and secure the service (latency, error rates, token counts). Such telemetry will not be used to train models unless Customer has opted into the feedback program."

4) Attribution / Derivatives: include explicit carve-out that product features derived from internal Redwood model improvements remain Redwood IP; derivative works based solely on Customer Content remain Customer IP.

I've attached a short redline bundle with clause snippets. If Aurelia requires strict title for all Outputs (no model-transformation carve-outs), that's a negotiation point — it materially restricts how we can productize features for other customers and may be an enterprise-only concession.

Proposed next steps:
- Confirm whether Aurelia needs unilateral title for all Outputs or if the license approach is acceptable.
- If strict title is required, ops needs to review SLA/price impacts (dedicated capacity, restricted telemetry).
- Sync Monday 10:00am PT as Nikhil proposed.

Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel, Contracts & Privacy
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Draft order form + a few questions on output ownership and training

Laura / Nikhil — thanks for the quick turnaround and the options. A few clarifications from Aurelia legal/procurement:

- Our preference is clear title to Outputs generated from our data. The risk we run internally is downstream productization by teams that won't accept "license-only" uncertainty.
- On training: Aurelia's firm requirement is no training on Customer Content unless we explicitly sign an opt-in agreement. Aggregated telemetry for service health is OK as long as it is retained no longer than 90 days and cannot be re-associated to customer data.
- Attribution: we're flexible on Redwood retaining model IP, but need to ensure there are no hidden rights to derivatives that could affect our product roadmap.

If the compromise requires additional fees (e.g., dedicated environment / no telemetry), please flag that to procurement so we can budget accordingly.

We can take the license text you proposed to our GC, but if you can provide the specific redline language that asserts full Customer title (for their review) that would help speed approval.

-Beth

Beth — appreciate the clarity. Summary and mutual action plan below so procurement/GCs have a single doc to act on.

Mutual Action Plan (target dates):
- Today (1/12): Redwood provides two redline snippets — (A) Customer-Title-unilateral language and (B) License-with-guardrails language. (attached)
- Tue (1/13): Aurelia GC to advise which path they prefer and flag any non-starters.
- Wed (1/14): Redwood legal to produce final OA redline for chosen path.
- Tue (1/20): Target PO / procurement approval (Aurelia).
- Wed (1/21): DocuSign send for signature.

Commercial/operational notes:
- If Aurelia requires unconditional Customer title for all Outputs + strict no-telemetry, this will trigger an enterprise-only configuration (dedicated capacity and additional compliance work). Pricing impact: TBD; ops will scope once GC confirms.
- Standard path (license + no-train-by-default + opt-in feedback program) is covered under our hosted offering with no additional fee.

Proposed redline snippets (included in attached doc):
--- SNIPPET A (Customer Title) ---
"Customer retains exclusive title to all Outputs derived from Customer Content. Redwood hereby assigns to Customer any right, title and interest it may have in such Outputs and shall not use Customer Content to train or improve any Redwood models without Customer's prior written consent."

--- SNIPPET B (License + guardrails) ---
"Customer is granted a perpetual, worldwide, royalty-free, transferable license to use Outputs for any internal or commercial purpose. Customer Content remains Customer's property. Redwood will not use Customer Content or Outputs to train, fine-tune, or improve Redwood models without Customer's explicit, written opt-in to a separate feedback agreement. Redwood may collect aggregated, non-identifiable telemetry for operational purposes only, retained no longer than 90 days."

Next steps: I'm attaching the two snippets and a short redline OA for each path. Please confirm which path your GC prefers and we'll convert to full redline OA. If you prefer SNIPPET A (title), please confirm willingness to discuss dedicated capacity / pricing or let us know if you want Redwood to quote a dedicated/no-telemetry option.
